([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 14 | draft_team = [[Golden State Warriors]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–present | team1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years2 = [[2021-22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022-23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | highlights = * [[NBA champion]] ([[2022 NBA Finals|2022]]) * [[Associated Press|AP]] honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2021]]) * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2021) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] (2021) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2021) }} '''Moses Josiah Moody''' (born May 31, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. Moody was drafted 14th overall in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the Warriors. During his rookie season with the team, he won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]]. ==Early life== Moody began playing high school basketball for [[Parkview Arts and Science Magnet High School]] in [[Little Rock, Arkansas]], where he helped his team reach the state championship game in his freshman season.{{cite web |title=Moses Moody inks with Razorbacks |url=https://www.thv11.com/article/sports/moses-moody-inks-with-razorbacks/91-cee3135a-efc1-4e30-9030-79eaab3e8319 |publisher=[[KTHV]] |access-date=July 8, 2020 |date=April 17, 2020}} As a sophomore, he moved to [[North Little Rock High School]] in [[North Little Rock, Arkansas]]. Moody averaged 18.6 points, 7.2 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 2.1 steals and 1.4 blocks per game, leading his team to the Class 7A state title.{{cite web |last=Parker |first=Zach |title=Moody shines as NLR pays back Northside |url=https://www.hotsr.com/news/2018/mar/09/moody-shines-as-nlr-pays-back-northside/ |website=[[Hot Springs Sentinel-Record]] |access-date=July 8, 2020 |date=March 9, 2018}} He was named to the ''[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]'' All-Underclassman Team and the Arkansas 7A All-State Team.{{cite web |last=Davenport |first=Richard |title=Moses Moody feels the love from Arkansas staff and fans |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2019/oct/20/moses-moody-feels-love-arkansas-staff-and-fans/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=July 8, 2020 |date=October 20, 2019}} For his junior year, Moody transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]]. He averaged 17.7 points, 3.9 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.6 steals per game for Bradley Beal Elite at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) regular season and was named to the All-EYBL honorable mention.{{cite web |last=Davenport |first=Richard |title=ESPN's Biancardi: A lot to like about Moses Moody |url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/nov/09/lot-about-moses-moody-said-espns-paul-biancardi/ |website=[[The Northwest Arkansas Times]] |access-date=July 8, 2020 |date=November 9, 2019}} In his senior season, Moody averaged 11.6 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game for Montverde, the consensus number one team in the nation, who he helped achieve a 25–0 regular season record. Moody received several high major [[NCAA Division I]] scholarship offers as early as his sophomore season.{{cite web |last=Davenport |first=Richard |title=NLR's Moody more of complete player since beginning of the season |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2018/mar/04/nlrs-moses-moody-more-complete-player-beginning-se/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=July 8, 2020 |date=March 4, 2018}} He finished high school as a consensus four-star recruit in the 2020 class. On November 9, 2019, Moody committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] over offers from [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], among others. He became the highest-ranked player to commit to Arkansas since [[Bobby Portis]] of the 2013 class.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=November 9, 2019 |title=Moses Moody, No. 29 in ESPN 100, picks Arkansas over Michigan |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28044301 |access-date=July 8, 2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} {{College Athlete Recruit |url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2021/mar/14/moody-makes-28-his-own/ |website=WholeHogSports |access-date=July 20, 2021 |date=March 14, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 16.8 points and 5.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web |date=April 9, 2021 |title=Arkansas Razorbacks guard Moses Moody declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31224097 |access-date=July 20, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]]}} Moody earned [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] and First Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] honors.{{cite web |last=Hutchinson |first=Andrew |title=Moody, Notae earn postseason SEC honors |url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/moody-notae-earn-postseason-honors-from-sec |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=July 20, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021}} After helping Arkansas to a 25–7 overall record, an Elite Eight appearance in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]], and a Top Ten finish in the polls, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] on April 9, 2021, forgoing his remaining college eligibility. ==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2021–present)=== Moody was selected with the 14th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite news |last=Letourneau |first=Connor |title=Warriors draft Jonathan Kuminga at No. 7, Moses Moody at No. 14 |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/Warriors-take-G-League-Ignite-s-Jonathan-16350815.php |access-date=July 30, 2021 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |date=July 30, 2021}} On August 5, 2021, Moody signed with the Warriors.{{cite web |date=August 4, 2021 |title=Warriors Sign Jonathan Kuminga and Moses Moody |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-kuminga-moody-20210805 |access-date=August 6, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} On October 19, Moody made his debut in the NBA, coming off the bench with two points and two rebounds in a 121–114 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Curry, Warriors stun James, Lakers 121-114 in opener|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401358774|date=October 19, 2021|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 19, 2021}} On January 11, 2022, on assignment with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]], Moody scored 37 points in a 132–130 overtime victory over the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Cody |title=Warriors' Moses Moody erupts for 37 points in G League |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/01/11/warriors-moses-moody-nba-g-league-stats/ |access-date=February 6, 2022 |work=Rookie Wire |date=January 11, 2022}} On March 7, Moody scored a career-high 30 points in a 131–124 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/lists/nba-twitter-reacts-to-warriors-falling-short-in-gritty-performance-vs-nuggets/|title=NBA Twitter reacts to Warriors falling short in gritty performance vs. Nuggets|last=Call|first=Tommy|website=USA Today|date=March 7, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2022}} On June 16, he won the [[2022 NBA Finals]] with the Warriors.{{cite web |date=June 17, 2022 |title=NBA Finals 2022: Complete news, schedules, stats for Golden State Warriors vs. Boston Celtics |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33714756 |access-date=December 31, 2024 |website=[[ESPN]]}} On October 20, 2024, Moody signed a three-year, $39 million extension with the Warriors.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |last2=Andrews |first2=Kendra |author-link2=Kendra Andrews |name-list-style=and |date=October 20, 2024 |title=Warriors extend Moses Moody on 3-year, $39 million deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41911629 |access-date=October 21, 2024 |website=ESPN}} He played in 74 games (34 starts) for Golden State during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.8 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Warriors' Moses Moody undergoes surgery on injured right thumb|url=https://www.nba.com/news/warriors-moses-moody-surgery-thumb-injury|access-date=June 2, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} On April 30, 2025, during the first round of the playoffs, Moody recorded 25 points, nine rebounds, two assists and two steals in a 131–116 Game 5 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |title=VanVleet and Thompson lead the way as Rockets avoid elimination, routing Warriors 131-116 in Game 5 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401767912 |access-date=May 1, 2025 |website=ESPN}} On May 22, Moody underwent surgery to repair a torn [[ulnar collateral ligament of thumb|ulnar collateral ligament]] in his right thumb.{{cite web | last=Youngmisuk | first=Ohm | title=Warriors' Moody has surgery on torn thumb UCL | website=ESPN.com | date=2025-05-22 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45273179/warriors-moses-moody-surgery-repair-torn-ucl-thumb | access-date=2025-12-06}} Moody made 60 appearances (49 starts) for Golden State during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging career-highs in points (12.1), rebounds (3.3), assists (1.6), and steals (1.0). On March 23, 2026, in a game where the Warriors defeated the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]] 137–131 in overtime in [[Dallas]], Moody suffered a non-contact injury late in the game. Medical evaluation confirmed that the wing player sustained a left patellar tendon tear, ending his season early.{{Cite web |last=Slater |first=Anthony |date=Mar 24, 2026 |title=Moses Moody out for season with torn patellar tendon in knee |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48298800/sources-warriors-moody-torn-patellar-tendon-knee}} ==Personal life== Moody is the son of Kareem and Rona Moody.
